final_text:
graphs in the output are separated by a single "" entry.
  - Multiple consecutive blank lines collapse to one separator. No leading or trailing "" entries are produced.
- Never split URLs:
  - Words starting with "http://" or "https://" are treated as atomic.
  - If such a URL is longer than the width, it is placed on its own line instead of being chunked.
  - Shorter URLs are wrapped normally (i.e., placed in lines where they fit).

Implementation notes
- I added a small helper wrap_paragraph(ptext) that wraps a single paragraph while enforcing the URL rule and the greedy wrapping/splitting behavior for non-URL words.
- Paragraph input preserves logical grouping by joining non-blank input lines with single spaces before wrapping.
- Defensive removal of any trailing separator is performed to guarantee no trailing "".

Quick examples (from local test)
- wrap("This is a test\n\nNew para here", 10) -> ['This is a', 'test', '', 'New para', 'here']
- wrap("\n\nLeading blank lines removed\n\n", 10) -> ['Leading', 'blank', 'lines', 'removed']
- wrap("short http://example.com/very/long/url/path that follows", 10) -> ['short', 'http://example.com/very/long/url/path', 'that', 'follows']
- wrap("wordwithnospacesbutveryverylong", 8) -> ['wordwith', 'nospaces', 'butveryv', 'erylong']
